research_question: Does explainable source-quality-based selection produce a better and/or more efficient domain-specific RAG knowledge base than an equivalent random-source baseline?
supersedes: source-selection-experiment-v1 (frozen; instrument failure: 34/36 sources scored an identical 0.4525 under the v1 scorer, so top-N degenerated into alphabetical selection)

instrument_fix.validation_summary: 36/36 unique content_relevance values and composites on the frozen 36-URL pool; evidence passages semantically audited; two prior iterations rejected by evidence audit (blended-query embedding mismatch, then Wikipedia navbox boilerplate masquerading as coverage) and fixed before validation.

hypotheses.H1: QUALITY_SELECTED corpora (top-N by v2 content-aware composite) achieve higher retrieval metrics (Recall@K, MRR, NDCG) on the frozen benchmark than RANDOM_BASELINE corpora of the same N, on the common answerable-question subset.
hypotheses.H2: QUALITY_SELECTED corpora reach equal-or-better metrics with fewer documents/chunks/corpus characters than RANDOM_BASELINE (efficiency).
hypotheses.H0: Selection strategy makes no difference in the metrics above.
hypotheses.honesty_note: With N small relative to the pool, coverage (how many benchmark questions are even answerable in a corpus) may dominate retrieval metrics; coverage is reported strictly separately and cross-strategy metric comparisons are made only on common answerable-question subsets.

variables.independent: source-selection strategy: QUALITY_SELECTED (top-N by v2 composite score) vs RANDOM_BASELINE (uniform random with fixed seed)
controlled: evaluation benchmark (frozen automobile-engineering-baseline-v1 questions, strict mode, keyword fallback disabled)
dependent: Recall@3/5/10, Precision@3/5/10, MRR, NDCG (chunk basis; doc-recall recorded)
coverage: answerable questions per corpus (reported separately, never mixed into metrics)
selected source ids + v2 signals (content_relevance, domain_coverage, confidence, composite)

candidate_pool.provenance: identical to source-selection-experiment-v1.json candidate_pool (36 real Wikipedia URLs, all verified HTTP 200 at design time)

selection_scores.method: v2 scorer run in the runner over the same cached page content; composite = content_relevance*0.40 + domain_coverage*0.20 + authority*0.15 + accessibility*0.10 + source_type*0.05 + recency*0.05 + duplication*0.05

protocol.runs: 6 corpora: QUALITY_SELECTED x N in {5,8,11} and RANDOM_BASELINE x N in {5,8,11}
protocol.corpus_build: per run: create KB -> analyze-domain (deterministic mock spec) -> discover sources (real probes) -> ACCEPT selected -> ingest -> index with controlled chunking config
protocol.ground_truth: frozen benchmark questions translated per corpus via deterministic chunk content_hash; document GT via source URL; benchmark file never modified; questions with no translated GT are excluded as unanswerable and listed
protocol.evaluation: strict mode (allow_keyword_fallback=false), top_k in {3,5,10}, per-run evaluation run ids recorded
protocol.comparison_rule: cross-run metric comparisons only on the intersection of answerable questions; the intersection is reported explicitly

frozen_baseline.ground_truth_caveat: Ground truth is agent-authored, human review pending. Every metric in this experiment inherits that limitation and must not be presented as publication-grade until a human has reviewed the benchmark selections.
